cover.title: Project Kestrel: acquisition of a specialist testing laboratory group
cover.sub: We ask the committee to approve an equity commitment of ${eq}M at {mult}x EBITDA, with exclusivity ending on 21 November.
cover.meta: November 2026 · Fictional company, fund and figures, theme specimen

exec.title: Approve Kestrel: a base case of {moic}x and {irr}% that clears our hurdle in three of four cases

kpis.label: Gross IRR, base case, five-year hold
Entry EV / EBITDA, last twelve months

rows.p: Sign at {mult}x on last-twelve-month EBITDA of ${ebitda0}M. If the committee does nothing, exclusivity lapses and the seller reopens the process.

rows.h: Grow by buying, earn by owning
rows.p: Add regional labs at lower multiples than ours and move their testing onto Kestrel's accredited methods. EBITDA reaches ${ebitda5}M in year five.
Public utilities are {cust}% of revenue under contracts that reprice every three years. The downside case assumes the next repricing goes against us.

exec.source: Source: Kestrel management accounts; deal team model (all fictional)

chart.title: EBITDA growth carries {grow_share}% of the gain, so the return does not need a higher exit multiple

exhibit.title: Equity value bridge, base case, entry to year-five exit

bullets: Organic growth and four bolt-on labs lift EBITDA from ${ebitda0}M to ${ebitda5}M.
We underwrite the exit half a turn below entry, a cost of ${w2_abs}M.
Cash flow repays ${w3}M of debt over the hold.
takeaway.sowhat: The deal works on earnings growth alone; multiple expansion is not in the case.

chart.source: Source: deal team model, base case (fictional)
chart.note: Note: gross of carried interest; fees and costs include transaction and monitoring fees.

table.title: Three of four cases clear the {hurdle}x hurdle, and the severe downside returns the equity

exhibit.title: Returns by case at a five-year exit

table.callout: The severe downside assumes EBITDA flat on entry and a {cm3}x exit, and still returns the ${eq}M of equity: the debt amortises from cash flow in every case.
more: The downside case is the one we would defend to our own investors: it takes the utility repricing against us and assumes two of the four bolt-ons do not close. It still clears the cost of the fund's capital over the hold, though not the hurdle.
table.note: Note: base case governs. Management case shown for reference only; it assumes the full bolt-on pipeline closes.
